quests.title: A proper welcome
quests.summary: Iona needs two or three messages for the new sign beside the tram steps. Work payment: 25 p.
lesson: Each printed line becomes a message. Debug previews the card; Apply routine installs it.
Your program runs once. The sign repeats the installed card every four seconds.
Use two or three different messages, each at most 32 Latin letters, numbers or punctuation.
You can use ordinary print calls, or collect strings in a list and use the same for loop as the workshop.
hints: What happens if you print a second line?
Each printed line adds a page. A list and for loop also work.
quests.done: The welcome sign is running. Work payment: 25 p.

quests.title: After the light
quests.concept: if, else and a Boolean condition
quests.summary: Nell is home. The shop’s dusk relays have their condition backwards. Repair both daylight routines. Work payment: 18 p.
starter: # The lamps passed Nell’s bench test. Read the condition.
lesson: Nell checked the bulbs and relays. The bug is in the decision: the dark branch asks for no light.
world.time.is_dark is a Boolean: True after dusk, False in daylight. An if condition ends with a colon.
Python runs the indented lines below if only when the condition is True. Otherwise it runs the indented else branch. Keep the for loop: both lamps need the same rule.
The slate tests this page once in daylight and once in darkness. Apply routine installs both instructions. The clock chooses between them from then on.
Make the lamps off in daylight and on in darkness. An always-on routine passes an evening glance, but fails the daylight check.
hints: Follow one lamp through the starter: when is_dark is True, which set_lit call runs?
Switch the values in the two branches: True below if; False below else. Keep their indentation.
quests.done: Both lamps follow the shared clock. Nell has recorded 18 p for the closing round.
